steps.text: In a blender, combine the oil, vinegar, sugar, dill weed, salt, onion powder, garlic powder, dry mustard and pepper. Blend until smooth, cover and refrigerate until chilled.

raw_recipe.headline: Dill Vinaigrette
raw_recipe.description: Red wine vinegar, dill, onion and garlic powder, and mustard blend to make this simple to prepare vinaigrette.
raw_recipe.name: Dill Vinaigrette

recipeInstructions.text: In a blender, combine the oil, vinegar, sugar, dill weed, salt, onion powder, garlic powder, dry mustard and pepper. Blend until smooth, cover and refrigerate until chilled.

review.reviewBody: Wonderful dressing - I used olive oil instead of veg. oil and dijon instead of dry mustard. Very refreshing and was perfect over mixed greens. This would also be great over pasta salad as well.
Excellent - I used fresh dill instead of dried and let it infuse in the dressing for several hours.

I used EVOO instead of veg. oil, converted the dill to fresh, omitted the onion powder since I didn't have, used Dijon rather than dried mustard, reduced the sugar to 1 t., and I used the blender. Then I tripled it. It was great.

Light dressing, perfect for summer
Lots of flavor, I put over pastina & diced cucumbers & halved grape tomatoes, yum! I garnished with fresh dill
Yum!

Great recipe...I modified it sllightly due to our tastes, but it is awesome, easy & most people probably always have these ingredients on hand. Why buy salad dressing, this is much better. I used fresh dill in quantity rather than dill weed, & added a bit more oil (a little olive oil) and sugar as my family thought the vinegar was a bit strong. The blender method is the best part adding the oil last and slowly blending it in makes it perfect and it does not separate. A definite keeper, which is also easily modifiable to use different herbs from your garden...ie. tarragon, savory, etc. Would be 5 stars, but made a few changes.

Tasty. I quadrupled the recipe so I'd have enough for a few days. I also made a few other changes, using a combination of 75% EVOO and 25% canola oil, substituting Splenda for sugar, and using only half the amount of sweetener called for in the original recipe. I used it over a simple salad of leafy greens, cucumbers, green onions and tomatoes. It will go on a spinach salad tomorrow. My partner and I both agreed that this recipe is a keeper. Edited on 12/19/15 to add: I made it several times as above, but tonight I made the recipe as is except for substituting EVOO for the vegetable oil. Though it was sweeter, it was also an acceptable level of sweetness for some salads. Wonderful to have such a tasty recipe that is so easy and uses ingredients I always have on hand.
This is just what I wanted. I used fresh dill, dijon, and only about 1/2 of the sugar.

I really liked this but instead of adding all of the sugar, I added a tiny bit and if I thought it needed more I would add a tiny bit more, I saw the comments where people cut the sugar in half and I just thought to myself that I'm not one for sugary dressings or salads so I did it my way and I used maybe a quarter of what the recipe called for. I added candied walnuts on top so it really didn't need any sugar. I also switched out the oil with evoo.
Loved this dressing. Recipe called for too much sugar for my taste, so cut back by 1/2 teaspoon & added fresh lemon juice. It made a perfect dressing for my pasta salad!

10.1.20 I found this a bit on the bland side, and there was barely a hint of dill weed. I used olive oil, but it just tasted too oily to me; the spices were totally in the background. I added more vinegar and dill weed. This was just OK, doubtful I’d make again.

I made a number of changes to this recipe which not only suited my tastes, but I believe made this better - olive oil, not vegetable oil, no sugar, fresh dill (although dried would have been fine) and white wine vinegar rather than red. Light and delicious, a dressing that supports the salad rather than dominating it. My four star rating is WITH the above changes.
I liked this recipe. I used dried dill, I think it would be better with fresh.
Delicious! We had it on a romaine and salmon salad, but I can also see just tossing some cherry tomatoes in it. I used a little squirt of Dijon mustard instead of dry mustard.
I loved this dressing over mixed greens!
It was too sweet (and I cut the sugar in half) and lacked flavor in general. I won't be making this again.
Very good dressing, easy to make. I did cut back on the sugar by 1/2.
Easy to make and full of flavor but seemed to need something else or more of something.

This is my go to dressing and I love it! I do make a couple of minor changes. I withhold the dry mustard and use white pepper instead of black. This is a fabulous recipe and after trying many I hit pay dirt with this one.

I liked this quite a bit. My only real complaints were that the dill was a bit muted for my tastes and I think it was a little too sweet. Those are easy fixes for the future, though.

It doesn't strike me as a great dressing for cold lettuce salads (though I haven't tried it, so I could be wrong!), but I used it on a slightly warm no-fish Niçoise salad and it was fantastic.
I didn't have red wine vinegar on hand so I used white. It was delicious. Great with tomato and cucumbers...mmmm
